title: Go forward into what was promised. Turning back is the loss.
subtitle: Musa calls his people to the next step
then: Ibn Kathir explains that Musa ordered his people to enter the Holy Land and {reward}promised them victory if they went forward.{/reward} The land had been promised to the believers among them. The warning was clear: {trap}turning back would make them losers.{/trap}
now: The course you signed up for and then stopped attending. The apology you drafted and never sent. {trap}Walking away feels safe in the moment.{/trap} The verse says {idea}the loss is in turning back, not in the step forward.{/idea}
old: If I do not try, at least I cannot fail.
new: Turning back from what Allah opened for me is itself the failure.
try: Pick one good thing you abandoned halfway. Take one small step back toward it today.

title: We will go in once it gets easy.
subtitle: The excuse that waits for the obstacle to vanish

row.title: I will, once it is easy

then: Ibn Kathir says their excuse was that the people in the town were {trap}mighty, strong and huge{/trap}, and they could not stand against them. So they set a condition: {trap}we will enter once they leave.{/trap} They wanted the promise without the step.
now: I will start praying when work calms down. I will give charity after the loan is paid. I will fix things with my brother once he calls first. {trap}Waiting for the giants to leave.{/trap} {idea}They rarely leave on their own.{/idea}
old: I will do the right thing once the obstacles are gone.
new: The obstacle is part of the test, not a reason to wait.
try: Name one good thing you keep postponing until it gets easier. Do two minutes of it today.

title: Two men said: go through the gate, and rely on Allah.
subtitle: The few voices of courage in a fearful crowd
then: When the people refused, {idea}two righteous men{/idea}, named by Ibn Abbas and others as Yusha' son of Nun and Kalib son of Yufna, urged them on. These men {idea}feared Allah{/idea}, and Allah had blessed them. Their advice: {reward}enter through the gate and you will win, and rely on Allah.{/reward}
now: A meeting where everyone agrees to cut a corner. A family gathering where everyone joins in gossip. {trap}Being the only voice feels impossible.{/trap} Two people were enough here. {idea}You can be one of them.{/idea}
old: If everyone else is afraid, I have no right to speak up.
new: Fear of Allah can make me one of the few who says: let us go forward.
try: Today, be the one who says the kind or honest thing in a group, even quietly.

title: You and your Lord go fight. We will sit here.
subtitle: When people want the result but send others to do it

row.title: never
sub: as long as they are there

then: Even after the two men spoke, the people refused again, more bluntly. {trap}Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are staying right here.{/trap} They wanted the promised land, but {trap}wanted Musa and his Lord to win it for them.{/trap}
now: The group project where you let others do the work and put your name on it. The community fundraiser you share online but never give to. {trap}Watching from the couch.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks where your own effort is.{/idea}
old: Others are better at this. Let them handle it, and I will join later.
new: Leaving all the effort to others while I wait is the attitude this verse warns against.
try: Find one shared task at home or work you have been leaving to others. Do your part today.

title: I only have myself and my brother.
subtitle: A leader's honest prayer when people walk away

row.title: only myself
sub: and I bring it to Allah

then: After his people refused twice, Musa did not argue or force them. He turned to Allah: {idea}My Lord, I have power only over myself and my brother.{/idea} He asked to be {trap}separated from the people who openly disobeyed.{/trap}
now: You tried to keep the family together, to bring a friend back to prayer, to fix your team. {trap}They will not move.{/trap} Musa's words fit your mouth too: {idea}I only control myself.{/idea} Bring the rest to Allah.
old: If people around me do not change, I have failed.
new: I answer for myself, and I can bring the rest to Allah in prayer.
try: Make one honest dua tonight about someone you cannot change. Tell Allah you have done your part.

title: Forty years of wandering, and do not grieve.
subtitle: The cost of refusing the open gate

row.title: years of wandering
sub: lost, not sure where to go

then: Ibn Kathir says they were punished for forty years by being {trap}lost, wandering in the land, unsure where to go.{/trap} It was the result of refusing the command. Musa was told {idea}not to grieve{/idea} over people who had made their own choice.
now: Years of going in circles in the same job, the same habit, the same argument, {trap}because you said no to one hard step.{/trap} The wandering is not the end. {idea}Today's step can still be taken.{/idea}
old: Saying no to a hard step only costs me a little time.
new: Refusing the open gate can cost years, so I take the step while it is open.
try: Ask yourself which hard step you have been circling around. Write it down with a date.

title: Allah only accepts from those who are mindful of Him.
subtitle: Two brothers, two offerings, one envious heart
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {trap}the evil end of transgression, envy and injustice.{/trap} One brother's offering was accepted and the other's was not. Abu Ad-Darda' said that knowing Allah accepted {idea}even one prayer from me is better than this world and all in it{/idea}, because of this line.
now: Your colleague gets the promotion. Your sibling gets the praise. {trap}The thought arrives: why them and not me?{/trap} The verse turns you back to your own offering: {idea}is it done with a mindful heart?{/idea}
old: When someone else is blessed, something has been taken from me.
new: Their acceptance takes nothing from me. My work is to make my own offering sincere.
try: When envy comes today, make a short dua for that person's blessing to increase.

title: Even if you raise your hand, I will not raise mine.
subtitle: Strength held back by fear of Allah
then: Abdullah bin Amr said: {idea}by Allah, Habil was the stronger of the two, but fear of Allah held back his hand.{/idea} He refused to commit the same sin he was threatened with. Ibn Kathir says he chose {reward}patience and endurance.{/reward}
now: Someone insults you in the comments. A driver cuts you off and shouts. {trap}Your hand is already typing the reply.{/trap} The stronger son of Adam showed another kind of strength: {idea}I will not answer harm with the same harm.{/idea}
old: If I do not hit back, I look weak.
new: Holding back for Allah's sake is the stronger choice, not the weaker one.
try: The next time someone provokes you today, wait one full minute before responding, or do not respond.

title: The one who wrongs carries both burdens.
subtitle: The weight of a wrong falls on the one who does it
then: The brother who held back told the other that he would {trap}carry my sin and your sin.{/trap} Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and others said this means {trap}the sin of killing me, on top of your earlier sins.{/trap} He was warning his brother, still trying to stop him.
now: Someone spreads a lie about you at work. It feels like you are the one losing. {idea}But the weight of that wrong is on them, not on you.{/idea} Your job is to keep your own hands clean.
old: When someone wrongs me, I am the one who loses most.
new: A wrong lands heaviest on the one who commits it, so I keep my side clean.
try: Think of someone who wronged you. Leave the account with Allah and drop the replay in your head.

title: His own soul made the crime look reasonable.
subtitle: How the self talks a person into ruin
then: His brother had warned him, yet Ibn Kathir explains that {trap}his conscience encouraged him, making it seem like a sensible thing to do.{/trap} So he killed him and became {trap}one of the losers{/trap}, in this life and the next.
now: It is only a small lie. Everyone does it. They deserved it. {trap}The self is a skilled lawyer.{/trap} Before a wrong deed, it builds the argument. {idea}Notice when you start explaining to yourself why something wrong is fine.{/idea}
old: If I can explain it to myself, it must be okay.
new: My soul can make wrong look reasonable, so I check its arguments against Allah's guidance.
try: Catch one excuse you tell yourself today. Say it out loud and ask if it would hold before Allah.
